newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent falls on worries over U.S. products.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent falls on worries over U.S. products.

text.p: Brent December crude futures were lower at the close of business on Thursday, pushed by a sell off on NYMEX over worries about a rise in heating oil stocks in the U.S.
December last traded at $23.80 per barrel, down 27 cents from London on volume of 488 lots. January was off 19 cents at $23.22 on volume of 150 lots.
Brokers said worries about softer oil products markets in the U.S. were prompting sales of crude futures. Both London and New York crude futures fell overnight.
NYMEX December crude, which fell 67 cents in New York to $24.86, was last traded on the after-hours ACCESS system at $24.55 on good after-hours volume.

Heating oil tumbled in New York after the Energy Information Administration published data Wednesday supporting day-earlier findings from the American Petroleum Institute that distillate stocks were growing in the key east coast area.
This was another bearish factor, adding to extra U.S. pipeline capacity and higher refinery runs for distillates.
